ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ABCD$ is a square with side length $1$, and $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle. Then,what is the area of $\triangle BPD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, \\
draw PE $\perp$ CD and PF $\perp$ BC, \\
since the side length of square ABCD is 1, and $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
therefore $\angle PBC=\angle PCB=60^\circ$, PB=PC=BC=CD=1, \\
therefore $\angle PCE=30^\circ$, \\
thus PF=PB$\cdot \sin60^\circ=1\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, PE=FC=$\frac{1}{2}$, \\
$S_{\triangle BPD}=S_{\text{quadrilateral} PBCD}-S_{\triangle BCD}=S_{\triangle PBC}+S_{\triangle PDC}-S_{\triangle BCD}$ \\
=$\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times1+\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\times1-\frac{1}{2}\times1\times1=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}}$;

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ABCD$ is a square with side length $1$, and $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle. Then, what is the area of $\triangle BPD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: \textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, draw $PE \perp CD$ and $PF \perp BC$. Since the side length of square $ABCD$ is $1$, and $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle, therefore $\angle PBC=\angle PCB=60^\circ$ and $PB=PC=BC=CD=1$. Therefore $\angle PCE=30^\circ$. Thus $PF=PB\cdot \sin 60^\circ=1\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, and $PE=FC=\frac{1}{2}$. $S_{\triangle BPD}=S_{\text{quadrilateral }PBCD}-S_{\triangle BCD}=S_{\triangle PBC}+S_{\triangle PDC}-S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times1+\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\times1-\frac{1}{2}\times1\times1=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}}$.

Thus $PF=PB\cdot \sin 60^\circ=1\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, and $PE=FC=\frac{1}{2}$. $S_{\triangle BPD}=S_{\text{quadrilateral }PBCD}-S_{\triangle BCD}=S_{\triangle PBC}+S_{\triangle PDC}-S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times1+\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\times1-\frac{1}{2}\times1\times1=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ABCD$ is a square with side length $1$, and $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle. Then, what is the area of $\triangle BPD$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, draw $PE \perp CD$ and $PF \perp BC$. Since the side length of square $ABCD$ is $1$, and $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle, therefore $\angle PBC=\angle PCB=60^\circ$ and $PB=PC=BC=CD=1$. Therefore $\angle PCE=30^\circ$. Thus $PF=PB\cdot \sin 60^\circ=1\times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, and $PE=FC=\frac{1}{2}$. $S_{\triangle BPD}=S_{\text{quadrilateral }PBCD}-S_{\triangle BCD}=S_{\triangle PBC}+S_{\triangle PDC}-S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times1+\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}\times1-\frac{1}{2}\times1\times1=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{4}}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a square, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; point P is located inside the square near the upper part, line segments PB and PC together with the bottom side BC form triangle BPC, and BD and PD are also drawn in the figure, so what is required is the area of triangle BPD. Reasoning: By the coordinate method, let B=(0,0), C=(1,0), D=(1,1). Because the side length of the square is 1, BC=1; and because triangle BPC is an equilateral triangle constructed inward into the square with BC as a side, P=(1/2, sqrt(3)/2). The area of triangle BPD is 1/2 * |det(P-B, D-B)| = 1/2 * |(1/2)*1 - (sqrt(3)/2)*1| = 1/2 * (sqrt(3)/2 - 1/2) = (sqrt(3)-1)/4.
